title: Open extension preserves finite constructibility and its cohomological interval
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$, and $n\geq1$; put $P_n=A/t^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $V$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact), let $j:U\hookrightarrow V$ be an open immersion, and assume that $\ell$ is invertible on $V$ [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites and constant coefficient ring sheaves $(P_n)_U,(P_n)_V$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $j_!$ denote exact extension by zero on module sheaves and its termwise functor on their unbounded derived categories [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed, lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. For integers $a\leq b$ and $C\in D^b_c(U,P_n)$ in the finite-torsion sense [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], suppose $\mathcal H^r(C)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-cohomological-support]. Then $j_!C\in D^b_c(V,P_n)$ and $\mathcal H^r(j_!C)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$. More precisely, for every $r$ one has $\mathcal H^r(j_!C)\cong j_!\mathcal H^r(C)$; any finite constructible locally closed stratification for $\mathcal H^r(C)$ on $U$, together with a reduced closed complement $Z=V\setminus U$, is a constructible locally closed stratification on $V$ on which this sheaf is locally constant with finite stalks, with zero restriction on $Z$. Empty strata may be omitted.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.7, preservation by the open factor; Stacks proetale.tex Tags 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open) and 09BN (lemma-open-immersion)

proof.text: For every affine open $W\subseteq V$, the open subscheme $W\cap U$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], applied to the Noetherian scheme $V$. Thus $j$ is quasi-compact by the affine-open criterion in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Choose the reduced induced closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ on the closed set $V\setminus U$: by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], $i$ is a closed immersion with image $V\setminus U$ and $Z$ is reduced. For the constant ring sheaf $(P_n)_V$, [lem-pur-proetale-constant-coefficient-comparison] identifies its inverse images on $U$ and $Z$ with $(P_n)_U$ and $(P_n)_Z$. Hence the open-closed module identities of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] apply with precisely the coefficient sheaves of the statement.

source.place: Tags 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), 09BN (lemma-open-immersion); qc open and reduced complement hypotheses

proof.text: The functor $j_!$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Apply [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] to obtain its termwise functor on the unbounded derived categories. If $K^\bullet$ represents $C$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $H^r(j_!K^\bullet)\cong j_!H^r(K^\bullet)$ for every integer $r$, naturally in the representative. In particular an acyclic complex remains acyclic and a quasi-isomorphism remains a quasi-isomorphism. The isomorphisms therefore give $\mathcal H^r(j_!C)\cong j_!\mathcal H^r(C)$ in the localized category, independently of the representative.

Fix $r$ and any given finite stratification $U=\coprod_\alpha S_\alpha$ witnessing constructibility of $F=\mathcal H^r(C)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Its strata remain locally closed in $V$: if their images are $O_\alpha\cap T_\alpha$ with $O_\alpha$ open and $T_\alpha$ closed in $U$, write $T_\alpha=U\cap\overline T_\alpha$ with $\overline T_\alpha$ closed in $V$. Then $O_\alpha$ is open in $V$ and the image is $O_\alpha\cap\overline T_\alpha$ [def-weil-locally-closed-subset]. The immersion $S_\alpha\to U$ factors as a closed immersion into an open of $U$; that open is open in $V$, giving the same immersion into $V$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The minimal-closed-subset property of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] implies the descending-chain condition: the set of terms of any descending chain has a minimal member, after which it is constant. Thus $|V|$ is Noetherian. By [def-weil-constructible-subset], every locally closed subset of $V$ is constructible. This applies both to the images of $S_\alpha$ and to the closed subset $|Z|$. These subsets are disjoint and cover $V$, so, with the indicated immersions, they form a finite constructible locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification].

source.place: Tag 005L (lemma-constructible-Noetherian-space); properties.tex Tag 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology); explicit extension of the partition

proof.text:
For the immersion $s_\alpha:S_\alpha\to U$, the canonical constant-coefficient composition isomorphism [lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition] and the open unit isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] give
$$(j\circ s_\alpha)^*(j_!F)\cong s_\alpha^*(j^*j_!F)\cong s_\alpha^*F.$$
Here the inverse-image rings are identified by [lem-pur-proetale-constant-coefficient-comparison], so the isomorphisms are isomorphisms of $(P_n)_{S_\alpha}$-modules. On the complementary stratum the same open-closed node gives $i^*(j_!F)=0$. No assertion about geometric stalks on the boundary is needed.

source.place: Tag 09BN and complementary restriction vanishing; sites-modules.tex Tag 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules)

proof.text: On $S_\alpha$, compose each local constant-model isomorphism for $s_\alpha^*F$ with the isomorphism of step 4. This uses exactly the same covering and constant module, and induces isomorphisms on all geometric stalks; their finiteness is unchanged. On $Z$, the zero module sheaf is constant with value the zero $P_n$-module: its constant presheaf is already the zero sheaf, and every stalk is the one-element zero module [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Consequently the stratification of step 3 witnesses constructibility of $j_!F$. The cohomology isomorphism of step 2 transports these same witnesses to $\mathcal H^r(j_!C)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].

source.place: Lemma 6.7.7, open factor; finite-stage stratification argument supplied explicitly

proof.text: If $r\notin[a,b]$, then $\mathcal H^r(C)=0$ by hypothesis, hence $\mathcal H^r(j_!C)\cong j_!0=0$ by step 2; an additive functor preserves the zero object. Thus the cohomological support stays in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-cohomological-support]. This interval contains only finitely many integers, and all cohomology sheaves are constructible by steps 3--5, so $j_!C\in D^b_c(V,P_n)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. If $U=\varnothing$, the only stratum needed is $Z=V$ with the zero sheaf; if $U=V$, omit the empty complement. Empty original strata can also be omitted, since none contributes points or a nonvacuous restriction condition.

from.place: Integral construction: preservation of finite constructible reductions by the open factor, extracted from original step 6

split_report.summary: Proved finite-stage open constructibility directly by extending each given stratification by the reduced complement, using canonical constant coefficients and the ringed open-closed identities. Exact-functor cohomology gives the same interval on the unbounded derived category. All ingredients already have nodes; no new nodes. Checked boundary, empty open/complement, arbitrary Noetherian schemes and nonregular finite coefficient rings.
split_report.blueprint: Nearest ancestor def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support: integral construction, preservation of finite constructible reductions by the open factor (original step 6), via lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible. The current main-20261015 version remains the same integral compact-support construction; no unit route is replaced.

tool_uses.why: Generic exact module extension by zero and its open/closed restriction identities, for arbitrary ring sheaves. This unit has no replacement proving these ringed identities; its compact-support route uses them as a black box.

Generic existence of the reduced induced closed subscheme on the closed complement, needed for the reduced complement Z in the statement; the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme gives a closed subscheme with that image but does not state reducedness.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NI-55f37f240 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery against Bhatt–Scholze 6.7.7 (p. 56, which only gives a proof sketch) and Stacks proetale 09AH and 09BN. I also confirmed the 010N, 005L, 01OZ, 03D8 and 015F labels. There are no new nodes. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from NP's version, and there is no repair note, so this is a first split (6 steps, 4585 characters). All arguments of the base Q34 step 6 are kept and expanded. Step 1: j is quasi-compact (W∩U is Noetherian by the open-subscheme leaf). Step 2: constant-coefficient comparison, then H^r(j_!K) ≅ j_!H^r(K) through the exact-functor leaves. Step 3: strata that are locally closed in U are locally closed in V, the immersions compose, minimal elements give a Noetherian space, and 005L inside def-weil-constructible-subset gives constructibility. Steps 4–5: pullback composition plus j^{-1}j_!=id and i^{-1}j_!=0 give the same local models, with zero on Z. Step 6: the cohomology interval is kept. Edge cases checked: U empty, U=V, V empty, C=0, n=1, non-reduced V. There is no cycle, uses equal proof_deps, and no SGA is cited. Not a duplicate: the open-extension constant-model node has a field base, sfb-dc is lfp, and sf-open-ctf and trf-open-ctf need finite type plus Tor. Accepted tool use: lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed. FIX, C4: step 1 claimed a reduced induced complement by citing lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme, which states no reducedness. I replaced it with clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, updated uses and proof_deps, and declared it in tool_uses.
